label: inflorescence type
definition: An inflorescence phenotype that characterizes the inflorescence by the branching pattern of its axes, the determinacy of those axes, and the manner in which its flowers are attached to them.

label: inflorescence type spike
definition: An inflorescence type phenotype in which the inflorescence is an unbranched, indeterminate axis bearing sessile flowers along its length.

label: inflorescence type raceme
definition: An inflorescence type phenotype in which the inflorescence is an unbranched, indeterminate axis bearing pedicellate flowers along its length.

label: inflorescence type umbel
definition: An inflorescence type phenotype in which all flowers or their pedicels arise from a single point at the apex of the inflorescence axis.

label: inflorescence type panicle
definition: An inflorescence type phenotype in which the inflorescence has a main axis with lateral branches that are themselves further branched, each axis ending in a flower or flower bud.

label: inflorescence type head
definition: An inflorescence type phenotype in which more or less sessile flowers are densely clustered on a short, often broadened inflorescence axis.

label: inflorescence type cyme
definition: An inflorescence type phenotype in which the main axis terminates in a flower and the inflorescence grows further only by lateral branches that each also terminate in a flower.

label: inflorescence type solitary
definition: An inflorescence type phenotype in which flowers are borne singly and are not grouped with other flowers into a multi-flowered inflorescence.

label: inflorescence type fascicle
definition: An inflorescence type phenotype in which several flowers arise in a close bundle from nearly the same point on a very short or undeveloped inflorescence axis.

label: petal free
definition: A petal structure phenotype in which the petals of a flower are not united with one another, each petal being attached separately to the receptacle.

label: tepal fused
definition: A tepal phenotype in which the tepals of a flower are united with one another, at least at their bases, so that the perianth forms a tube or cup.

label: tepal free
definition: A tepal phenotype in which the tepals of a flower are not united with one another or with any other floral organ.

label: fruit type
definition: A fruit phenotype that characterizes the fruit by the consistency of its pericarp, the number of carpels and seeds from which it is formed, and whether and how it opens at maturity.

label: fruit type capsule
definition: A fruit type phenotype in which the fruit is dry, dehiscent, and derived from two or more carpels.

label: fruit type legume
definition: A fruit type phenotype in which the fruit is dry, derived from a single carpel, and dehiscent along two longitudinal lines.

label: fruit type follice
definition: A fruit type phenotype in which the fruit is dry, derived from a single carpel, and dehiscent along one suture only.

label: fruit type berry
definition: A fruit type phenotype in which the fruit is indehiscent and fleshy or pulpy throughout, with one or more seeds embedded in the fleshy pericarp.

label: fruit type drupe
definition: A fruit type phenotype in which the fruit is indehiscent and derived from a single carpel, with a fleshy outer pericarp and a hard, stony endocarp enclosing the seed.

label: fruit type nut
definition: A fruit type phenotype in which the fruit is dry, indehiscent and one-seeded, with a hard pericarp, and is derived from two or more carpels.

label: fruit dehiscence
definition: A fruit phenotype that characterizes whether the mature fruit opens to release its seeds.

label: fruit dehiscent
definition: A fruit dehiscence phenotype in which the mature fruit opens along definite lines or pores to release its seeds.

label: fruit indehiscent
definition: A fruit dehiscence phenotype in which the mature fruit does not open to release its seeds, which are dispersed while still enclosed in the fruit.

label: fruit winged
definition: A fruit shape phenotype in which the fruit bears one or more flat, thin, membranous or papery outgrowths of its wall.

label: whole plant lifeform
definition: A whole plant phenotype that characterizes the plant by its growth form, in particular by the position of its perennating buds relative to the soil surface during the unfavourable season and by the substrate on which it grows.
sources: Raunkiaer C. (1934) The Life Forms of Plants and Statistical Plant Geography. Oxford: Clarendon Press.|PO:0000003

label: whole plant therophytic
definition: A whole plant lifeform phenotype in which the plant completes its life cycle within a single favourable season and survives the unfavourable season only as seed.
sources: Raunkiaer C. (1934) The Life Forms of Plants and Statistical Plant Geography. Oxford: Clarendon Press.|PO:0000003

label: whole plant cryptophytic
definition: A whole plant lifeform phenotype in which the perennating buds of the plant lie below the soil surface or under water during the unfavourable season.
sources: Raunkiaer C. (1934) The Life Forms of Plants and Statistical Plant Geography. Oxford: Clarendon Press.|PO:0000003

label: whole plant geophytic
definition: A whole plant cryptophytic phenotype in which the plant perennates by an underground storage organ, such as a bulb, corm, tuber or rhizome, from which the aerial shoots are renewed annually.
sources: https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?alpha=G&glossary=yes&page=nswfl#geophyte|Raunkiaer C. (1934) The Life Forms of Plants and Statistical Plant Geography. Oxford: Clarendon Press.|PO:0000003

label: whole plant helophytic
definition: A whole plant cryptophytic phenotype in which the perennating buds lie in waterlogged soil or mud, while the flowering and leafy shoots rise above the water surface.
sources: Raunkiaer C. (1934) The Life Forms of Plants and Statistical Plant Geography. Oxford: Clarendon Press.|https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?alpha=E&glossary=yes&page=nswfl#emergent|PO:0000003

label: whole plant hydrophytic
definition: A whole plant cryptophytic phenotype in which the plant grows submerged in water, sometimes partly emergent, and its perennating buds lie under water.
sources: https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?alpha=H&glossary=yes&page=nswfl#hydrophyte|Raunkiaer C. (1934) The Life Forms of Plants and Statistical Plant Geography. Oxford: Clarendon Press.|PO:0000003

label: whole plant hemicryptophytic
definition: A whole plant lifeform phenotype in which the perennating buds of the plant lie at the soil surface, where they are protected by soil, litter or the dead remains of the shoots.
sources: Raunkiaer C. (1934) The Life Forms of Plants and Statistical Plant Geography. Oxford: Clarendon Press.|PO:0000003

label: whole plant chamaephytic
definition: A whole plant lifeform phenotype in which the perennating buds of the plant are borne on persistent shoots close above the soil surface, typically below about 25 cm.
sources: Raunkiaer C. (1934) The Life Forms of Plants and Statistical Plant Geography. Oxford: Clarendon Press.|PO:0000003

label: whole plant phanerophytic
definition: A whole plant lifeform phenotype in which the perennating buds of the plant are borne on persistent aerial shoots well above the soil surface, as in trees and shrubs.
sources: Raunkiaer C. (1934) The Life Forms of Plants and Statistical Plant Geography. Oxford: Clarendon Press.|PO:0000003

label: whole plant epiphytic
definition: A whole plant lifeform phenotype in which the plant grows perched on another plant, using it for support without being parasitic on it.

label: whole plant litophytic
definition: A whole plant lifeform phenotype in which the plant grows on rock surfaces or in rock crevices rather than in soil.

label: whole plant graminoid
definition: A whole plant herbaceous phenotype in which the plant has the habit of a grass, sedge or rush, with long, narrow, parallel-veined leaves and small, inconspicuous flowers.

label: whole plant forbacious
definition: A whole plant herbaceous phenotype in which the plant is a non-woody plant other than a grass, sedge or rush.

label: shoot axis woodiness
definition: A shoot axis phenotype that characterizes the degree to which the stem is hardened by lignified secondary xylem.

label: tissue succulence
definition: A portion of plant tissue phenotype that characterizes the degree to which the tissue is thickened and fleshy because it stores water.

label: tissue succulent
definition: A tissue succulence phenotype in which the tissue is thick, fleshy and water-storing.

label: whole plant ecology
definition: A whole plant phenotype that characterizes the plant by its relationship to its environment or to other organisms, such as its mode of nutrition or its habitat.

label: whole plant parasitic
definition: A whole plant ecology phenotype in which the plant grows on another living organism, the host, and obtains water or nutrients from it.

label: latex presence
definition: A plant latex phenotype that characterizes whether the plant exudes latex, a usually milky fluid, from cut surfaces of its leaves and stems.

label: latex present
definition: A latex presence phenotype in which a usually milky fluid is exuded from cut surfaces of the leaves or stems of the plant.

label: latex absent
definition: A latex presence phenotype in which no latex is exuded from cut surfaces of the leaves or stems of the plant.

label: whole plant with stingy hairs
definition: A whole plant hairy phenotype in which the plant bears hollow hairs seated on glands that secrete an irritating fluid.

label: whole plant flower position
definition: A whole plant phenotype that characterizes the part of the plant body, such as the current leafy shoots, older branches or the trunk, on which flowers are produced.

label: whole plant cauliflorous
definition: A whole plant flower position phenotype in which flowers or fruits are produced on the trunk or on major, well-developed branches.

label: whole plant ramiflorous
definition: A whole plant flower position phenotype in which flowers or fruits are produced behind the current foliage, on woody branches formed in previous seasons.

label: leaf rosulate
definition: A leaf spatial pattern phenotype in which the leaves are clustered in a radiating rosette, usually close to the ground at the base of the plant.

label: leaf palmately compound
definition: A leaf shape phenotype in which the leaf is compound, with three or more leaflets arising from a single point at the top of the petiole.

label: leaf pinnately compound
definition: A leaf shape phenotype in which the leaf is compound, with its leaflets arranged in two rows along a rachis.

label: leaf foliolate
definition: A leaf shape phenotype in which the leaf is divided into leaflets, the ultimate segments of a compound leaf.

label: leaf base cordate
definition: A leaf base shape phenotype in which the leaf base is heart-shaped, with a notch at the point of attachment of the petiole.

label: leaf vascular system palmate
definition: A leaf vascular system shape phenotype in which several primary veins radiate from a single point at the base of the leaf lamina.

label: leaf vascular system triplinerve
definition: A leaf vascular system shape phenotype in which three prominent primary veins diverge from the midvein slightly above the base of the leaf lamina.

label: leaf vascular system parallel
definition: A leaf vascular system shape phenotype in which the primary veins of the leaf lamina run in the same direction and at about equal distances from one another.

label: leaf margin crenate
definition: A leaf margin shape phenotype in which the leaf margin bears shallow, rounded teeth.

label: leaf margin subentire
definition: A leaf margin phenotype in which the leaf margin is almost neither toothed nor dissected, bearing at most a few minute or obscure teeth.

label: fused corolla present
definition: A fused corolla phenotype in which the petals of the flower are united by their margins, at least at the base, so that the corolla is a single structure.

label: fused corolla absent
definition: A fused corolla phenotype in which the petals of the flower are free from one another, so that the corolla does not form a single united structure.

label: flower style length
definition: A flower phenotype that characterizes the length of the style, the part of the carpel between the stigma and the ovary.

label: pedical ciliate
definition: A pedicel ciliatedness phenotype in which the stalk of the flower is fringed with fine hairs resembling eyelashes.

label: whole plant lifestyle
definition: A whole plant phenotype that characterizes the plant by the duration of its life cycle from germination to fruiting and death.

label: whole plant annual
definition: A whole plant lifestyle phenotype in which the plant completes its life cycle, from germination to fruiting, within one year and then dies.

label: whole plant biennial
definition: A whole plant lifestyle phenotype in which the plant completes its life cycle, from germination to fruiting, in more than one but less than two years and then dies.

label: whole plant perennial
definition: A whole plant lifestyle phenotype in which the life span of the plant extends over more than one growing season, the plant usually flowering and fruiting repeatedly.

label: bract margin membranous
definition: A bract margin texture phenotype in which the bract margin is thin and translucent.

label: whole plant architecture
definition: A whole plant phenotype that characterizes the overall spatial organization of the plant body, including its branching pattern and the arrangement of its shoot axes.

label: hasValue
definition: A data property that relates an amount quality to the integer number of entities that the quality measures, as used in FLOPO count phenotypes.
